pages.title: At the doctor

unit.name: Health & body
map: Asking for help in an emergency

situation.text: You have a sore throat and you are at a doctor’s office in the United States. You check in, say what is wrong and answer the doctor’s questions.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can say what is wrong, say how long you have had it and ask one question to the doctor — clearly and politely.
canDo: Say: I have a… (a sore throat, a cough, a fever)
Say how long: since Monday / for three days
Check in with your name and insurance card
pages.think: In Brazil, how do you tell the doctor what is wrong? Do you start with the problem or with a greeting?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo em voz alta e peça que o estudante diga com as próprias palavras o que fará hoje.
Pergunte “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz UMA palavra que associa à situação.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso: é a missão final da aula.
extra: Have you ever been to a doctor abroad?
What do you say first at a doctor’s office?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s day, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: At the pharmacy: “Do you have something for…?” Ask: What do you ask a pharmacist when you have a cough?

qs.q: Do you go to the doctor often?
qs.pt: Você vai ao médico com frequência?

qs.q: Is there a clinic near your home?
qs.pt: Tem uma clínica perto da sua casa?

pages.tip: Keep the talk about habits and places, not about the student’s real health problems. Nobody has to share private health information.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto e retomar a aula anterior.
extra: What is a good question for the doctor?
How do you make an appointment where you live?

errors.r: I’ve had a cough for three days.

errors.w: I am with a sore throat.

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Doctor visits in the USA
pages.intro: Going to the doctor in the USA has small steps: appointment, check-in, waiting room, then the exam room. Look and guess.

cards.note: Many people call or use an app before going.
At check-in, you often show your ID and insurance card.
You check in at the front desk and wait until they call your name.

qs.q: What do you do when you arrive?
qs.pt: O que você faz ao chegar?

levels.A2: I check in at the front desk.
levels.B1: I check in, show my ID and insurance card and wait.
levels.B2: You usually check in, hand over your documents, fill out forms and wait to be called.

qs.q: What does the doctor ask first?
qs.pt: O que o médico pergunta primeiro?

levels.A2: The doctor asks what the problem is.
levels.B1: The doctor asks what’s the matter and how long you have had it.
levels.B2: Typically, the doctor asks about your main concern and how long it has been going on.

qs.q: Why is a waiting room useful?
qs.pt: Por que a sala de espera existe?

levels.A2: You sit and wait for your name.
levels.B1: The office is busy, so you wait until the doctor is ready.
levels.B2: It organizes the flow of patients, and you may wait even with an appointment.

pages.compare: In Brazil, many people also wait in a waiting room and show a card or ID. What is the same and what is different where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com o que conhece do Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: check in no balcão, documentos, esperar.
Q2: What’s the matter? / How long…?
Q3: sala de espera organiza a fila de pacientes.
extra: Do you carry an ID card to the doctor?
What do people do in a waiting room?

errors.w: How long time you have it?
errors.r: How long have you had it?

support: Use as respostas do nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: compare convenções sociais no Brasil e nos EUA.

pass1.q: Why is the man at the doctor?
pass1.pt: Por que o homem está no médico?
opts: He has a sore throat and a cough

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois 5 informações.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: as 5 informações da tarefa.
Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Compare respostas entre as duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 1: He has a sore throat and a cough
Pass 2: sore throat · cough · Monday · tired · insurance card
extra: Do you prefer a small clinic or a big hospital?
What word was new today?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

qs.q: What is the matter with Max?
What does the doctor ask him to do?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê um papel e você lê o outro; depois troquem.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: Sore throat and cough · Since Monday · Open his mouth · His insurance card
extra: Have you ever been to a doctor abroad?
What do you say first at a doctor’s office?

errors.w: I am sick of the throat.

support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.pt: O que você tem? / Qual é o problema?
items.use: The doctor asks about the problem.
Say what is wrong: a cough, a fever, a sore throat.

items.pt: Há quanto tempo você está com…?

items.use: A common question from the doctor.
The doctor gives a simple instruction.

items.pt: Aqui está o meu cartão do plano.

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Peça um exemplo próprio com cada ★.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Compare em duplas.
answers: Doctor’s question · Say a problem · Say the time · Ask about it · Paperwork
extra: What is a good question for the doctor?
How do you make an appointment where you live?

errors.r: I’ve had a cough for three days.

support: Trabalhe só as 3 primeiras expressões ★ nesta aula.

patterns.name: Ask about the problem
ex: What’s the matter with your throat?

patterns.name: Ask how long
ex: How long have you had it?
How long have you had a cough?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: What seems to be the problem?
I am experiencing a sore throat.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules.

teach.goal: Fixar os 2 padrões principais; os outros são expansão. Use a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo.
Use “Swap the words”: peça a frase completa a cada troca.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; os demais são expansão.
extra: Do you prefer a small clinic or a big hospital?
What word was new today?

errors.w: I am with a sore throat.
How long time you have it?
errors.r: How long have you had it?

support: Fique só com o padrão 01 na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine dois padrões na mesma fala.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — question intonation
pages.tip: Wh-questions usually go down at the end: What’s the matter? Yes/no questions usually go up: Do you have a fever? The goal is to be clear, not to remove your accent.

items.say: How long have you had it?
items.linked: How LONG have you had it? ↘

own.prompt: Write one question for the doctor and mark if the voice goes up or down.
own.criteria: Did your voice go down for wh-questions and up for yes/no questions?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: Intonation of questions.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e entonação → usar com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e normal; peça palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria com o fenômeno.
answers: Identify: What’s the matter? · Do you have a cough?

errors.w: What’s the matter? com tom subindo no final, como pergunta de sim/não
Do you have a fever? (voz desce)
errors.r: Do you have a fever? (voz sobe)

support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça a versão mais educada ou mais informal.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: Controlled: I have a sore throat. · Since Monday. · For three days. · Is it serious?
Guided: matter · have · I’ve had it for three days. · I’ve had it since Monday. · I think so. I feel hot.
extra: Have you ever been to a doctor abroad?

errors.w: How long time you have it?
errors.r: How long have you had it?

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — at the doctor

brief.teacher: You are the doctor. Ask “What’s the matter?” and “How long…?”. Do not diagnose or give advice: this is language practice. Change the plan during the scene.
brief.student: You are the patient: say what is wrong, say how long and ask one question.

orders: A cough and a sore throat
complications: The doctor asks you to repeat.
You forget the day it started.
You do not understand a word: ask for help.
The receptionist asks for your insurance card.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Use sintomas leves e fictícios; não peça dados reais de saúde do aluno.
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Fale ≤ 35% do tempo. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: Do you carry an ID card to the doctor?
support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça só a primeira frase.

rounds.title: What’s the matter?
rounds.task: Doctor and patient: say the problem.
rounds.hint: What’s the matter? / I have a…

rounds.title: How long?
rounds.task: Say how long you have had it.
rounds.hint: How long have you had…? / Since… / For…

rounds.title: Check in
rounds.task: Check in at the front desk with your name and insurance card.
rounds.hint: I have an appointment. / Here’s my card.

rounds.title: Share
rounds.task: Whole group: each pair says one good question.

infogap.title: Patient cards
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Card A
a.task: You know the problem and the day it started for Mr. Lee. Ask about the rest.

b.title: Card B
b.task: You know the fever and the appointment time for Mr. Lee. Ask about the rest.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada; com 6 estudantes, três duplas simultâneas.
Sem salas simultâneas: interações sequenciais enquanto uma dupla apresenta.
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
answers: A sabe: a cough, since Tuesday. B sabe: fever (a little), appointment at ten o’clock.
extra: Do you prefer a small clinic or a big hospital?
What word was new today?

errors.w: How long time you have it?
errors.r: How long have you had it?

support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — at the doctor
pages.goal: Each group must get through a doctor visit in English: check in, say what is wrong and say how long.

missions.mission: You have a cough. Say what is wrong, say since when and ask “Is it serious?”
Check in at the front desk with your name and insurance card, then tell the doctor you have a fever.
missions.constraint: Say your name and use “for three days”.

missions.mission: You have a sore throat. The doctor asks how long. Ask one question.
missions.constraint: Answer “How long?” with since or for.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “What’s the matter?” → “I have a cough.” → “How long have you had it?” → “For three days.”
extra: Have you ever been to a doctor abroad?
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a clinic. Say you have a sore throat, say since when and ask for an appointment.
pages.model: Hello! My name is Max Dias. **I have a sore throat and a cough.** I’ve had them since Monday. Can I make an appointment, please? Thank you!
checklist: I said my problem (I have a…).
I asked for an appointment and thanked them.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.
extra: What do people do in a waiting room?

errors.r: I’ve been sick since Monday. / I have a cough since Monday.

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You said the problem and the time clearly.
prompts.improve: Example: Raise your voice on yes/no questions.
prompts.next: Example: Check in and tell the doctor what is wrong without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask how long they have had it.
tasks.model: How long have you had it?

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: The doctor asks: “What’s the matter?” You have a cough.

items: Record a 45–60 second audio: you are a patient and say what is wrong.
Write a short message asking for an appointment.
Review three expressions and create your own examples.
Listen to the dialogue again and identify two expressions.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: How long have you had it? · I have a cough. · Since Monday.
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar na próxima aula, depois de uma semana e na missão de encerramento da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Say the problem with a simple phrase.

ladder.say: I have a sore throat. I’ve had it since Monday.
I’ve had a cough for three days and I’m a little worried about it.
ladder.goal: Describe a problem and a feeling.

ladder.say: I’d like to know whether this is something I should be concerned about.
It started out mild, but it has been gradually getting worse over the past few days.
I’d rather get it checked now than wait and wonder whether it will clear up on its own.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
